4.01.b:
### Hold it → side in 3 steps
1) **Down** → wide, cancellous **articular end** with scaphoid + lunate facets = distal
[[FIG: Fig 4.1 · 4.01
2) **Back** → **Lister's tubercle** + tendon grooves = dorsal; front smooth, concave
3) **Lateral** → the **radial styloid** reaches further distal than the ulnar styloid (Bontrager)

- **Side rule** → 3 steps above + **sigmoid (ulnar) notch** faces the ulna

### Point & say — distal radius and ulna
| Point to | What it is / attaches |
|---|---|
| Radial styloid | **BR** (brachioradialis) insertion; RSC (radioscaphocapitate) ligament origin |
| Lister's tubercle | EPL on its **ulnar** side; ECRL/ECRB (extensor carpi radialis longus/brevis) radial to it |
| Sigmoid notch | **DRUJ** (distal radioulnar joint) → TFCC (triangular fibrocartilage complex) attaches at its rim |
| **Watershed line** | Most volar radial ridge → capsule starts; plate past it → **FPL** (flexor pollicis longus) **rubs and ruptures** (Ashour; Operative sheet) |
| Ulnar head + **fovea** | Deep TFCC fibres (ligamentum subcruentum) → the DRUJ stabiliser |
| Ulnar styloid | Superficial TFCC fibres + ECU (extensor carpi ulnaris) sheath; 2–6 mm beyond the head (Campbell) |

- **Three columns** → each fails its own way, gets its own plate (Trauma sheet)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.2 · 4.01

| Column | Made of | Job | Fails → fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Radial | Styloid + scaphoid facet | Buttress against radial carpal shift | Shear → radial plate |
| Intermediate | Lunate facet + sigmoid notch | **Keystone**, main load path | Dorsal impaction → dorsal-ulnar plate |
| Ulnar | Ulnar head + TFCC | DRUJ stability, load in ulnar deviation | — |

- Load → **radius 80%, ulna 20%** in an ulnar-neutral wrist; ulna takes more if it is long (Orthobullets; Netter)

4.02.b:
### TFCC — parts and attachments
- Parts → **articular disc**, **dorsal + palmar radioulnar ligaments**, meniscus homologue, ECU sheath, ulnolunate + ulnotriquetral ligaments (Palmer 1981; Campbell)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.5 · 4.02
- Origin → sigmoid notch rim · insertion → **deep fibres → fovea**, superficial → styloid (Netter)
- No true wrist ulnar collateral ligament → the **ECU sheath** stands in (Netter)

MUST-KNOW — "iceberg" of the TFCC
- Distal "hammock" = disc + ulnocarpal ligaments → load cushion (Nakamura 1996)
- Proximal part → **foveal insertion** = the real DRUJ stabiliser (Atzei 2011)
- Foveal tear → severe DRUJ instability, even with a normal-looking disc (Nakamura 2011)
- Styloid tip fracture → foveal fibres usually spared; **base** fracture → suspect the fovea

### Blood supply and the Palmer zones
- Disc → avascular, aneural; periphery **10–25%** vascular (ulnar + anterior interosseous arteries) (Netter)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.6 · 4.02
- Rule → **peripheral tear repair · central tear debride** (Netter)

| Palmer class 1 (traumatic) | Site | Treatment idea |
|---|---|---|
| 1A | Central perforation | Debride (up to ≈80% of the disc, rim kept) (Hand sheet) |
| 1B | Ulnar avulsion ± styloid fracture | Repair (vascular) |
| 1C | Distal → ulnocarpal ligaments | Repair |
| 1D | Radial avulsion from the sigmoid notch | Debride / reattach |

- Class 2 = degenerative (ulnocarpal impaction) (Hand sheet; Palmer)
  - 2A thinning · 2B + chondromalacia · 2C hole · 2D + **LT tear** · 2E + arthritis

PITFALL — how much of the TFCC bleeds?
- Netter → outer 10–25%; Thiru 1986 → outer 15–20%
- Say → "**the outer fifth bleeds**, the centre does not"

### DRUJ stability
- Notch radius ≈15 mm vs head ≈10 mm → radius rotates **and slides**; bone gives only ≈**20%** of stability (Hand sheet; Campbell)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.7 · 4.02
- Contact ≈60% in neutral → 10–20% at full rotation → dislocates then (Hand sheet)
- Pronation 80°, supination 85°; axis radial head → fovea (Ashour) · classic → **dorsal radioulnar ligament tight in pronation, palmar in supination** (Netter)

| Forearm | Ulnar head sits | Forced → | Reduce + splint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pronation | Dorsal | Dorsal dislocation | Supinate → splint in supination 4–6 weeks |
| Supination | Volar | Volar dislocation | Pronate → splint in pronation |

- Irreducible → **ECU** blocks → open via the 5th compartment (Hand sheet)
- Other stabilisers → **ECU subsheath**, pronator quadratus, IOM (interosseous membrane) (Netter)
  - Rheumatoid → ECU slips volar → caput ulnae → Vaughan-Jackson rupture (Hand sheet)

4.03.b:
### Point & say the 8 bones
- Proximal row, radial → ulnar → **S**caphoid · **L**unate · **T**riquetrum · **P**isiform
  [[FIG: Fig 4.8 · 4.03
- Distal row → **T**rapezium · **T**rapezoid · **C**apitate · **H**amate
- Mnemonic → "**S**ome **L**overs **T**ry **P**ositions **T**hat **T**hey **C**an't **H**andle"

| Bone | Hold it → say |
|---|---|
| Scaphoid | Boat-shaped, **80% cartilage**, bridges both rows → #1 carpal fracture (60%), waist ≈66% (Netter; Hand sheet) |
| Lunate | Crescent, 4 joints (radius, scaphoid, triquetrum, capitate) (Netter) |
| Triquetrum | Pyramid under the pisiform → 3rd commonest carpal fracture (Netter) |
| Pisiform | Sesamoid in **FCU** (flexor carpi ulnaris) → TCL (transverse carpal ligament), ADM (abductor digiti minimi) (Netter) |
| Trapezium | Groove for **FCR** (flexor carpi radialis); saddle for the thumb (Netter) |
| Capitate | Largest, first to ossify, keystone, centre of rotation (Netter) |
| Hamate | **Hook** → TCL; deep ulnar nerve on it (Hoppenfeld) |

- Scaphoid tubercle → thumb axis meets the distal wrist crease (Hand sheet)
- Find the hook → thumb IP (interphalangeal) crease on the pisiform, tip toward the 1st web → hook under it (Hoppenfeld)

CLINICAL PEARL — hamate hook fracture
- Ulnar artery + **deep motor branch** lie on the hook → check both (Netter; Hoppenfeld)
- Golfers, batters → hypothenar-base pain → carpal tunnel view or CT (computed tomography)

### Ossification order
- **Counter-clockwise from the capitate**, about one a year (Netter)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.9 · 4.03
  - Capitate 1 → hamate 2 → triquetrum 3 → lunate 4 → scaphoid 5 → trapezium 5–6 → trapezoid 6–7 → **pisiform 9–10**
- Bone age → carpal count ≈ age in years, up to 6

### Scaphoid blood supply
- Dorsal scaphoid branch of the **radial artery** → **dorsal ridge** at the waist → **75%**, proximal part (Netter)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.10 · 4.03
- Palmar branch → tubercle → distal **25%** (Netter)
- Flow **retrograde** → waist fracture cuts off the proximal pole → AVN (avascular necrosis), nonunion (Netter)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "blood supply of the scaphoid"
- **Dorsal ridge** branch → 75%, proximal, retrograde · palmar → tubercle 25% (Netter)
- Micro-CT → dorsal ridge vessels in every specimen, **83%** of volume (Morsy 2019)
- AVN → ≈10% overall, ≈**50% in the proximal pole** (Hand sheet)
- Surgery → spare dorsal ridge soft tissue; central-axis screw harms least (Morsy 2019)

### Lunate types
- **Type I** → no medial facet for the hamate · **type II** → medial facet (Galley 2007)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.11 · 4.03
- Normal wrists → type II **63%**, type I 18% (Galley 2007)
- Kienböck → **71% type I** (Rhee 2015)
  - Lunate blood → 2–3 dorsal + 3–4 volar vessels (Gelberman 1980); single-vessel **I pattern** → highest risk (Hand sheet)

4.04.b:
### Extrinsic ligaments
- **Palmar** ligaments stronger, intracapsular; dorsal ones converge on the triquetrum (Netter; Orthobullets)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.12 · 4.04

| Group | Ligament | Point & say |
|---|---|---|
| Volar superficial | **RSC** | Styloid → capitate; scaphoid waist **sling**; keep it in PRC (proximal row carpectomy) |
| Volar superficial | **LRL** (long radiolunate) | Radius → lunate; proximal border of Poirier |
| Volar deep | SRL (short radiolunate) | Stout, vertical → holds the lunate |
| Volar deep | **Ligament of Testut** | Radioscapholunate → vessels only, no strength |
| Ulnar | UL, UT, UC | Ulnolunate, ulnotriquetral, ulnocapitate → ulnocarpal complex |
| Dorsal | **DRC** (dorsal radiocarpal) | Radius → triquetrum → main dorsal stabiliser |
| Dorsal | **DIC** (dorsal intercarpal) | Triquetrum → trapezium/trapezoid → forms the dorsal "**V**" with DRC |

- Count → **12 extrinsic** → volar radiocarpal 5, volar ulnocarpal 4, dorsal 3 (Hand sheet)
- **Space of Poirier** → weak area between LRL and RSC + UC at the capitate neck → **perilunate dislocations pass here** (Netter)

CLINICAL PEARL — keep the RSC
- **PRC** → RSC becomes the main capitate-on-radius stabiliser (Orthobullets)
- Large **radial styloidectomy** cuts its origin → carpus slides ulnar (Orthobullets)

### Intrinsic ligaments
- **SL** (scapholunate) → C-shaped → **dorsal part strongest** (260 N) > palmar (118 N) > proximal membrane (63 N) (Berger 1999)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.13 · 4.04
- **LT** (lunotriquetral) → **palmar part strongest** (Netter)
- Distal row → strong interosseous ligaments → moves as **one unit** (Netter)

MUST-KNOW — SL or LT? DISI or VISI?
- SL torn → scaphoid flexes, lunate **extends** → **DISI** (dorsal intercalated segment instability)
- LT + DRC torn → lunate **flexes** with the scaphoid → **VISI** (volar intercalated segment instability) (Netter)
- Static DISI → needs SL **+ DIC** off the lunate; SL cut alone not enough (Mitsuyasu 2004)
- Memory → "**S**L → lunate looks up (D) · **L**T → lunate looks down (V)"

### Rows, columns and motion
- Proximal row → **no tendon attachments** → **intercalated segment** moved by the rows around it (Netter)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.14 · 4.04
- Scaphoid pulls the lunate into flexion · triquetrum into extension → balance (Netter)
- Radial deviation → scaphoid flexes · ulnar deviation → extends (Orthobullets)
- Columns → lateral (mobile: scaphoid, trapezium, trapezoid) · central (flexion–extension: lunate, capitate, hamate) · medial (rotation: triquetrum) (Orthobullets)

| Motion | Normal | Mostly at |
|---|---|---|
| Flexion | 65–80° | Midcarpal 60% |
| Extension | 55–75° | Radiocarpal 65% |
| Radial / ulnar deviation | 15–25° / 30–45° | Midcarpal |

- Netter values; functional arc ≈10° flexion, 35° extension (Orthobullets)
- **Dart-thrower's motion** → radial-extension to ulnar-flexion, all midcarpal → functional plane; lost after midcarpal fusion (Hand sheet)

1) SL torn
[[FIG: Fig 4.15 · 4.04
2) Lunocapitate → capitate dislocates
3) LT torn → perilunate dislocation
4) Lunate dislocates volarly **through the space of Poirier** (Netter)

- **Lesser arc** = pure ligament · **greater arc** = through bone → transscaphoid perilunate is the commonest (Netter)
